question: 次の目標は 10 ＿びょう＿ です。
source_explanation:
びょう is written 秒 because 秒 means "second" (unit of time), fitting a time goal.
秒 (びょう) = second — the unit of time. The sentence says 「次 (つぎ) の目標 (もくひょう) は10秒 (びょう) です」 — "The next goal is 10 seconds." 秒 reads びょう (on-yomi). It is the smallest standard time unit in Japanese: 時間 (じかん, hour), 分 (ふん/ぷん, minute), 秒 (びょう, second). The kanji 秒 contains 禾 (grain) on the left and 少 (little) on the right — the tiny fraction of a grain measurement.
✗ 培 (ばい/つちか-う, to cultivate/nurture): 培 relates to growing or cultivating plants or skills. It reads ばい or つちかう, not びょう. 培 has no connection to time units.

question: ボールが遠くまで ＿とんだ＿ 。
source_explanation:
とんだ is written 飛んだ — the ball flew far.
飛ぶ (とぶ) is a kun-yomi verb meaning "to fly" or "to leap / to soar through the air". The n-form past 飛んだ (とんだ) expresses the completed action of something flying through the air. The sentence 「ボールが遠くまでとんだ」 means "The ball flew far." The kanji 飛 itself resembles a bird in flight — one of the most visually iconic kanji at N3. Its on-yomi ヒ appears in compounds: 飛行機 (ひこうき, airplane), 飛翔 (ひしょう, soaring). When 飛 stands as a verb, the reading is always と. question: このドラマの ＿つづき＿ が楽しみだ。

question: もう少し ＿あさい＿ 皿がほしいです。
source_explanation:
あさい is written 浅い because 浅い means "shallow", fitting a request for a shallower plate.
浅い (あさい) = shallow — having little depth. The sentence says 「もう少 (すこ) し浅 (あさ) い皿 (さら) がほしいです」 — "I would like a plate that is a bit shallower." This is a natural request when choosing tableware: a plate with a low rim versus a deeper bowl. 浅い is used for physical depth (浅い水, あさいみず, shallow water) and metaphorically for shallowness of thought or experience (考えが浅い, かんがえがあさい, shallow thinking).

question: この ＿しま＿ には、初めて来ました。

question: これが ＿いっぱんてき＿ な方法です。

question: 今日も ＿かならず＿ 行きます。
source_explanation:
かならず is written 必ず — 必 means "certainly / without fail" and ず is the negative auxiliary expressing inevitability.
必ず (かならず) = certainly, definitely, without fail. 「今日 (きょう) も必 (かなら) ず行 (い) きます」 — "I will definitely go today too." A very common adverb. Critical spelling note: the correct form is 必ず without ら; 必らず (with ら) is a well-known spelling error frequently tested on JLPT.

question: 効果が ＿あらわれた＿ ようですよ。
source_explanation:
あらわれた is written 現れた because 現 means "to appear / to manifest," which describes an effect becoming visible.

question: それは ＿ぎゃく＿ ですよ。
source_explanation:
ぎゃく is written 逆 — the kanji meaning "reverse / opposite".
逆 (ぎゃく) means "the opposite" or "the reverse". The sentence 「それはぎゃくですよ」 means "That is the opposite (of what you think)." Among the four options, 逆 is the only kanji that carries this meaning. Its on-yomi is ギャク, and its kun-yomi is さか, seen in the word 逆さ (さかさ, upside-down) or 逆上がり (さかあがり, a gymnastics move). The movement radical 辶 (しんにょう) on the left suggests motion, and the right side suggests going against a stream. Common N3-level compounds include 逆転 (ぎゃくてん, reversal) and 逆効果 (ぎゃくこうか, counterproductive effect).
✗ 途 reads と or みち.

question: あしたの朝は気温が ＿ひくく＿ なるそうです。
source_explanation:
ひくく is written 低く — tomorrow morning the temperature will be low.
低い (ひくい) is a kun-yomi adjective meaning "low" — in height, level, or temperature. The ku-form 低く (ひくく) is the adverb form. question: 毎日 ＿ねっしん＿ に勉強している。
source_explanation:
ねっしん is written 熱心 — 熱 means "heat/passion" and 心 means "heart".
熱心 (ねっしん) = enthusiastic/earnest (な-adjective). 「毎日 (まいにち) 熱心 (ねっしん) に勉強 (べんきょう) している」 — "I study enthusiastically every day." Geminate: ねつ + しん → ねっしん.

question: 授 業で花の 形や色を ＿かんさつ＿ しました。
source_explanation:
かんさつ is written 観察 — 観 means "to observe" and 察 means "to examine closely".
観察 (かんさつ) = careful, systematic observation. The sentence says 「授業 (じゅぎょう) で花 (はな) の形 (かたち) や色 (いろ) を観察 (かんさつ) しました」 — "In class, we observed the shape and color of flowers."

question: 中村さんは一週間前に ＿たいいん＿ したそうです。
source_explanation:
たいいん is written 退院 — 退 means "to leave / withdraw" and 院 means "hospital", meaning "leaving the hospital / being discharged".
退院 (たいいん) = hospital discharge — leaving the hospital after treatment. 退 (たい) = to retreat/leave, 院 (いん) = hospital/institution. question: もうちょっと ＿あつい＿ のが欲しいです。
source_explanation:
あつい is written 厚い — 厚い means "thick".
厚い (あつい) = thick. 「もうちょっと厚 (あつ) いのが欲 (ほ) しいです」 — "I would like something a little thicker."

question: 昨日の夜、3０分 ＿ていでん＿ した。

question: この文章を ＿やくして＿ もらえませんか。
source_explanation:
やくして is written 訳して because 訳 means "to translate," which is what you do when you convert text from one language to another.
訳す (やくす) means "to translate" — to convert text or speech from one language into another. Its te-form 訳して (やくして) appears in requests and instructions. The sentence says: "Could you translate 訳して (やくして) this passage for me?" The kanji 訳 has the on-yomi やく and the kun-yomi わけ. In verb form as 訳す (やくす), it uses the on-yomi やく. The meaning distinction between 訳す (translate) and 訳 as a standalone noun (訳 わけ, meaning/reason) is important: the same kanji serves both functions.

question: あそこにいるのが私の ＿むすめ＿ です。
source_explanation:

question: その話をしたら、彼女は ＿笑って＿ いました。
source_explanation:
笑って is read わらって because 笑う means "to laugh / to smile", fitting the description of her laughing after hearing the story.
笑う (わらう) = to laugh or to smile. Its て-form is 笑 (わら) って. The sentence says 「その話 (はなし) をしたら、彼女 (かのじょ) は笑 (わら) っていました」 — "When I told that story, she was laughing." 笑う is the kun-yomi used for the natural action of laughing. The on-yomi しょう appears in compounds like 苦笑 (くしょう, wry smile) or 失笑 (しっしょう, involuntary laugh).
✗ こまって: て-form of 困る (こまる, to be troubled/at a loss). Being troubled is not the same as laughing. 困 and 笑 are different kanji with opposite emotional tones.

question: 病院で ＿血液型＿ を調べました。

question: この時代の生活にどんな ＿変化＿ があったのか、調べてみたい。
source_explanation:

source_explanation:
通知 is read つうち — 通 reads つう and 知 reads ち, meaning "notification / notice".

question: 来年から ＿税金＿ が上がるそうだ。
